messages.author: 257e8e3417c1da26
messages.subject: Query on occupancy modelling
parts:
Can anybody answer these questions.

I am a postdoc at the University of KwaZulu-Natal working on the 17 years citizen science data on Cape parrots in South Africa which is called the Cape parrot big birding day (CPBBD). I wish to analyse this long-term data using the "unmarked" package to estimate the extinction and colonization probability of Cape parrots at a site/patch.  Every year Cape parrots are counted on  Sat morning and Sunday evening by volunteers and experts. Basically only 2 days a year since 1998. I have a few queries concerning the analysis of this data.

1.  If a site is visited once on Saturday morning and if the same site is visited on a Sunday evening within a gap of 24 hrs can this be considered as a repeated site visit. I will be adding weather, time of sampling as covariates. I would like to include repeated site sampling data rather than merging the data for the 2 days into 1 day. What are your suggestions on this?

2. Another issue is that the number of sites sampled during CPBBD have increased over the years meaning there is unequal effort across years. Could the sites having unequal effort be included in this analysis. For eg the data structure would look like this

        y1998 y1999 y2000
site1    1         1        0
site2     0        0        1
site3    NA     NA      1

3. In such data sets does it make sense to use the count data or presence/absence of the species? Surely number of observers have increased over the years which will be added as  a covariate too but in addition to this I would like to add other covariates that have changed over time for eg. land cover, tree cover, temperature along with site covariates like patch metrics.

4. If count data is a better option then could I use the N-mixture models?

Any suggestions on this will be highly appreciated.

Cheers
Riddhika



--
Dr. Riddhika Kalle
Postdoctoral Fellow
School of Life Science
University of KwaZulu-Natal
Scottsville
Pietermaritzburg

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Query on occupancy modelling
parts:
hi Riddhikalle,
 1. Yes you can use surveys on consecutive days (even hours, or minutes) . I would encourage you to read some of the literature on the models to understand the interpretation and how it might change as a function of the interval of sampling.

 2. unbalanced sampling is not, in general, a problem as long as you have some replication

 3. You could use the count data which sometimes are more informative than just presence/absence.  I would encourage you to explore the various types of models and then see which might be best to answer your specific questions.

 4. Yes the N-mixture models implemented in the pcount() function would be appropriate for count data.

regards,
andy
